name: Sand-cast iron (green-sand foundry casting)
process: The patternmaker carves the part in wood about one per cent oversize, with draft on every face so it will lift out of the sand. The moulder rams damp 'green' sand round the pattern in a two-part flask, lifts the pattern, sets cores for any hollows, cuts the runners and closes the mould. Iron remelted in a cupola is poured at about 1300 degC; once cold the casting is knocked out, the runners and fins broken off and the skin fettled. Parts are joined by bolted flanges and spigots; cast iron is not welded. The result keeps the mould's marks: a fine sand texture, parting lines, generous fillets, and a hard skin that resists corrosion.
